_what: The Emergent Future Worlds Meets Mountain Man, David's log cabin at the summit of the mountain that stands over the Campgrounds, off the main campsite. Helen Edgar's relay of his brief, 2026-10-18: a cabin on a mountain with a lake through the windows, the windows opening onto his photographs; a fire; a lounge; warm and cosy meets smart-home modern, LED strips that change colour, a big screen and speakers with his YouTube on it; an oil diffuser; one switch; one wolf inside and the pack outside under a full moon, with a button to hear them; coffee and cups; crisps, sweets and Skittles; and, the same morning, geothermal like Ryan's hermitage is solar, a hot spring outside, a cable car up so Ryan, Helen and Jess can visit, and wolves outside. tools/make-mountain-cabin.py writes the big screen and its rack, the wall and the window of photographs and the credits in liner-notes.html from this file. Do not hand-edit between the markers.
_source: The playlist was read off its own page on YouTube on 2026-10-18 (ytInitialData, whose rows came as lockupViewModel, the shape pull-live-month.py learned on 2026-10-15), and every video was asked on its own watch page the same day: playabilityStatus OK, playableInEmbed true, none of them LOGIN_REQUIRED, and the title, channel and length as that page gives them. The titles are the channels' own and are not swept. A runtime is the watch page's lengthSeconds, which can read a second shorter than the player's figure, because it is rounded down.
_drift: The rack is a mirror of the playlist and drifts by design: a video David adds is on the big screen the next time somebody puts the whole playlist on, and on the rack only when somebody reads the playlist again and adds a row here. The room prints the date this file was read, under the rack.

photos._what: David's own photographs. Every one needs its record in data/polaroids.json (on_wall false, elsewhere naming this page, David as photographer and his yes, nobody in it or everybody in it recorded) and its file in photos/, stripped of every byte of metadata, which tools/make-polaroids.py enforces for every photograph on the street. Each id here is a polaroids.json id, and the tool refuses one with no record or no file. Until a photograph is here with its record, the wall holds its frames and says so.

springs._what: Photographs of hot springs like the cabin's, beside the spring's words: not ours, not David's, and not of the cabin's own spring, which is drawn. Each is somebody's photograph on Unsplash under the Unsplash License, credited and linked by name and by picture, chosen by Helen Edgar on 2026-10-18, Where somebody is in one, far off and a stranger to this street, the room says so in the caption and the record says so here: Helen's call, 2026-10-18, to use Jeremy Mowery's anyway, credited and said. The file lives in borrowed/, the place for photographs that are somebody else's, saved through Pillow with every byte of metadata stripped; tools/make-webp.py measures it like every JPEG here.

photos.alt: A clear turquoise hot spring pool held in a rim of pale mineral rock, steam drifting off it, beside a wide shallow river with grass banks and a dark pine-covered hill under a cloudy sky.
photos.caption: A hot spring beside a river, something like the one outside the door. Photograph by Fabio Sasso, on Unsplash.

photos.people: Three people standing on a boardwalk on the far side of the pool, small and far off, strangers to this street whose yes nobody could ask; Helen Edgar's call to use it anyway, credited, with the room saying so.
photos.alt: A wide turquoise hot spring pool with steam drifting across it, its rim crusted pale and the ground round it bare and stony with small yellow flowers, a wooden boardwalk along the far side with three people standing on it, a lake beyond, and a line of mountains under a grey sky.
photos.caption: A hot spring pool like ours, somewhere else: steam off turquoise water, and three people on a boardwalk at the far side, strangers to this street and a long way off. Photograph by Jeremy Mowery, on Unsplash.

wolves_photos._what: Photographs beside the wolves' words, borrowed like the springs': credited, linked, licensed, and the caption saying what the animals in it are, because a photograph's own title is what it is and not what we would like it to be. Fetched from Unsplash's image host on 2026-10-18 with Helen's go-ahead, after the pictures she sent would not arrive as files.

photos.alt: A wolf walking through snow between dark tree trunks, its head low and turned to one side, its fur grey-brown on the back and cream on the face and legs, one yellow eye catching the light.
photos.caption: A wolf like the ones outside, somewhere else, in the snow. Photograph by Andrew Ly, on Unsplash.

photos.alt: Two huskies close together in dim light: one in profile with a dark mask, a pale blue eye and a white muzzle, the other facing the camera with brown eyes, both grey, cream and tan.
photos.caption: Two huskies, by the photograph’s own title: dogs and not wolves, though they look the part, which is why they are here. Photograph by Shavr IK, on Unsplash.
